Transcript Body:
[00:00] Jared (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm jared kim from redwood inference — happy to kick us off, we have priya on the se side and maya on customer success. how are you all?
[00:12] Elena (SummitWay): good thanks, we've got a few folks here, i'll hand over to derek to walk through our infra constraints.
[00:18] Derek (SummitWay): yeah hi, derek here. quick context: we run a hybrid cloud setup, primary workloads in us-east-1 but we'd like a private peering into a dedicated cluster for inference, and we have strict egress rules. also curious how redwood handles kv cache and prefix caching — sometimes people call it kay vee cache in notes — and how that maps to our subnet/security groups.
[00:42] Priya (Redwood SE): sure, thanks. so our private deployments (private control plane + customer-managed data plane) can sit in your VPC, we support routing via VPC peering or AWS Transit Gateway, and we'll need the peering CIDRs plus a small list of ports. for kv cache: at runtime the runtime maintains local kv caches on the GPU nodes — it's not an external service unless you opt into a shared cache tier.
[01:04] Nina (SummitWay): can you say more about encryption at rest? we use KMS and need to map keys to our HSM.
[01:10] Priya (Redwood SE): yep — we integrate with customer KMS via cross-account grants; you can bring your key material to the node level if you want HSM-backed keys. audit logs are shipped to your cloud logging account. there might be some transcriber noise where people say quantize or quantisation and the engine reads it as quantizashun — but the config is straightforward.
[01:36] Omar (SummitWay): timeline wise we're trying to run a 4-week pilot and production in 8–10 weeks. is that reasonable?
[01:42] Maya (Redwood CSM): totally reasonable — pilot scope usually takes 2–4 weeks with a staging cluster, followed by a ramp for production. we'll map milestones in the runbook.
[02:05] Elena (SummitWay): success criteria: latency p95 under 200ms for our 1k token prompts and cost per request below our current in-house infra baseline. also full auditability for all requests.
[02:22] Jared (Redwood): great — we'll capture that as pilot success criteria. quick Q: do you expect to use streaming responses or non-streaming?
[02:29] Derek (SummitWay): streaming, yes — our product needs near-real-time responses for the chat flows.
[02:34] Priya (Redwood SE): streaming has a small tail on throughput but it's supported; we'll size GPUS accordingly and advise on batching settings. a note: intelligent batching and prefix/KV cache reduce per-token cost but we need the request distribution.
[03:10] Nina (SummitWay): on compliance, we need SOC2 type II evidence and iso 27001 docs if available, and SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning. can you support SSO with just SCIM push?
[03:20] Maya (Redwood CSM): yes we do SAML + SCIM provisioning; we'll need your IdP metadata and a service account for SCIM. i'll send the SSO checklist.
[03:31] Derek (SummitWay): network question — do you prefer peering or TGW? we've heard both from other vendors.
[03:36] Priya (Redwood SE): TGW reduces maintenance but many customers choose peering for tighter control; both are supported. we'll recommend based on your VPC topology after we see the diagram.
[03:50] Elena (SummitWay): what about dedicated capacity vs hosted — cost tradeoffs?
[03:55] Jared (Redwood): dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; hosted is faster to start but you lose some isolation. for a security-sensitive pilot with SSO and KMS, Dedicated or Private deployment is a common choice. we'll model cost vs token throughput in the perf template.
[04:18] Omar (SummitWay): ok can you outline what's in the runbook?
[04:22] Maya (Redwood CSM): runbook includes contact matrix, network checklist, SSO/KMS steps, staging cutover, rollback steps, monitoring & alerting thresholds, and pilot success criteria. i'll drop a draft today.
[04:40] Derek (SummitWay): on observability — we need token-level latency traces and per-route dashboards. is that available?
[04:46] Priya (Redwood SE): yes — our console provides per-route latency, token counts, model breakdowns, and tracing hooks to forward spans to your tracing backend. we'll show examples in the next deep-dive.
[04:59] Nina (SummitWay): about logs — retention and PII redaction — we want logs to land in our logging account and redact pii upstream. do you support that?
[05:08] Priya (Redwood SE): logs can be pushed to your logging bucket; redaction is something we can configure with pre-shipping processors or you can handle it on your side. we'll align on retention windows.
[05:27] Jared (Redwood): quick note on model variants and fallbacks — we can route by policy (latency, cost) and have automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant if capacity is constrained. sometimes the transcript autoparsers call variants like redwood-serve or redwood-private incorrectly, so sorry for the noise.
[05:50] Elena (SummitWay): excellent. one more — do you have a white-glove onboarding for the pilot?
[05:55] Maya (Redwood CSM): yes we run weekly syncs plus a dedicated onboarding channel, and an ops playbook.
[06:05] Omar (SummitWay): can you run a baseline with our example payloads? we'll share a small dataset of typical prompts.
[06:11] Priya (Redwood SE): absolutely — send sample prompts and a concurrent user profile and we'll run a perf template to estimate latency and cost.
[06:22] Derek (SummitWay): regarding ports, which egress ports do you need again?
[06:26] Priya (Redwood SE): primarily TCP 443 for control-plane communications, and optional ports for metrics and tracing. i'll put a minimal list in the runbook.
[06:40] Elena (SummitWay): any blockers on security from your side before the deep dive?
[06:44] Nina (SummitWay): i'd like to see the SOC 2 narrative and where audit logs live. also encryption key lifecycle and any cross-account grants.
[06:53] Maya (Redwood CSM): we'll attach SOC2 summary and the KMS pattern doc to the runbook.
[07:02] Jared (Redwood): great — let's go through immediate dates: maya will send runbook draft by tomorrow, priya will produce perf baseline by monday, derek will share the VPC diagram by end of week; we should have a network deep dive scheduled next tuesday.
[07:20] Omar (SummitWay): sounds good. quick sidebar — do you support function/tool calling and structured outputs?
[07:27] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, function calling, structured outputs and streaming are all supported; we'll demo structured output examples in the integration session.
[07:40] Elena (SummitWay): ok i'm going to summarize for internal stakeholders: pilot success criteria (p95 <200ms, cost below baseline, full auditability), requirements (VPC peering/TGW, SAML+SCIM, KMS/HSM integration), deliverables (runbook, perf template, SOC2 summary). any corrections?
[07:57] Jared (Redwood): all correct — i'll record the next steps here.
[08:05] Derek (SummitWay): one quick thing — we sometimes hit tokenization differences across models; if you recommend model and quantization profile, please note expected regressions.
[08:15] Priya (Redwood SE): yes we'll include recommended models and quantization options with quality caveats.
[08:27] Elena (SummitWay): thanks everyone. last ask — can you confirm backup plan if peering takes longer than expected?
[08:34] Maya (Redwood CSM): fallback is hosted with IP allowlist and strict audit controls, we can use that to keep the pilot on track.
[08:45] Omar (SummitWay): perfect.
[08:49] Jared (Redwood): awesome thanks all — recap of next steps and i'll follow up with calendar invites for the network deep dive and perf check.
[09:00] Meeting end.
